gates.name: Official-source data integrity
gates.protects_against: a signal that is really a transcription error
gates.threshold: 100% of score and record fields recompute from the official schedule pages and match the official standings page; no cell inferred
gates.evidence: 192/192 club fields agree across 32 clubs and 137 finals (W, L, T, PF, PA, games). Aliases applied: ARI->AZ, LAR->LA, LAC->LAC, LV->LV, WAS->WAS.
gates.how_to_pass: already passing; re-run tools/verified_feed.py after any new capture

gates.name: Verified results feed exists
gates.protects_against: backtests and ROI computed on memory, screenshots or nothing
gates.threshold: every settled game has a final score traceable to an official page
gates.evidence: 137 finals in data/verified/results_2026.csv, each carrying its official week-page URL; 26 scheduled games deliberately carry no score.
gates.how_to_pass: already passing for weeks 1-10; extend by re-running the capture

gates.name: Minimum sample (corrected)
gates.threshold: at least 2272 settled bets at -110 before a 55% true edge is detectable at 80% power (exact binomial, one-sided); 498 for a 58% edge
gates.evidence: 0 settled bets exist. The published threshold of 300 bets is shown by exact power to be far too small: at 300 bets an 80%-power test only detects a true edge of 59.6% or better, which is far larger than any edge a model of this kind should be assumed to have. At 55% the requirement is 2272 bets.
gates.source: tools/selftest_stats.py verified against exact binomial enumeration
gates.how_to_pass: ingest settled results with prices, then accumulate; no shortcut exists

gates.name: Out-of-sample signal beats a naive baseline
gates.protects_against: a model that only looks clever
gates.threshold: walk-forward MAE below predict-zero and sign test p < 0.05
gates.evidence: MAE 9.29 vs 10.21 points on 89 unseen games; 56/88 correct sides, exact p=0.01375.
gates.how_to_pass: passing against predict-zero; the market comparison is G-5 and is blocked

gates.name: Edge over the market (CLV)
gates.protects_against: celebrating a signal the market already priced
gates.threshold: positive closing-line value on a pre-registered sample
gates.evidence: 0 of 39 market cells carry an official price. No official NFL price publication exists and no licensed feed is configured.
gates.how_to_pass: obtain a licensed price feed and record open and close per market

gates.name: Uncertainty reported with every number
gates.protects_against: a point estimate pretending to be a fact
gates.threshold: every published coefficient, rate and ROI carries n and a 95% interval
gates.evidence: 9 coefficients carry n, Fisher-z and a permutation p-value; bet-level ROI intervals are impossible while G-5 is blocked.

gates.name: Multiple-testing control
gates.protects_against: the best of many variants being reported as the finding
gates.threshold: Benjamini-Hochberg at 10% across every strategy evaluated in the window, with the number of variants disclosed
gates.evidence: 12 strategies registered, 0 evaluated on priced outcomes, 0 variants to correct.
gates.how_to_pass: run when at least one strategy has a priced sample

gates.name: Correlation from official numbers only, with n
gates.protects_against: multiplying parlay legs as if independent
gates.threshold: every joint-outcome coefficient printed with n and an interval, from officially sourced observations
gates.evidence: game total vs |margin| r=-0.0157 (n=137, CI -0.1829 to 0.1524, permutation p=0.85281) - the interval includes zero, so on this sample the two legs cannot be shown dependent. Prop-level joints remain blank.
gates.how_to_pass: prop joints need an official prop archive, which does not exist

gates.name: Capacity and cost
gates.protects_against: an edge that disappears at the price you can actually get
gates.threshold: net of vig and limits, edge remains positive at the intended stake
gates.evidence: no vig, limit or line-movement data exists in the repository.
gates.how_to_pass: requires the price feed from G-5

gates.name: Demotion gate (live -> paper)
gates.protects_against: a dead strategy kept alive by an early lucky run
gates.threshold: ANY of the triggers below sends the strategy back to paper on the next re-rating; no discretion, no vote
gates.evidence: 0 live strategies exist, so nothing can be demoted yet. The triggers are defined now so the rule cannot be written after a losing run starts.
gates.how_to_pass: n/a - this is a control, not a milestone

demotion_triggers.trigger: 30+ settled bets with negative cumulative flat-stake profit
demotion_triggers.why: A 12-bet losing run is normal, so the trigger is on cumulative profit over the run rather than on consecutive losses. Thirty bets is short enough to act on and long enough that a real edge rarely sits under water for all of it.
demotion_triggers.arithmetic: At a true 55% win rate, 30 losing bets in a row has probability 0.45^30 = 3.95e-11; at breakeven it is 2.15e-10. The trigger is therefore not a 50/50 call: it fires on a run that a genuine edge almost never produces.
demotion_triggers.source: computed here from the exact binomial; kernel verified by tools/selftest_stats.py

demotion_triggers.trigger: trailing 400-bet ROI below -3% while the pre-registered expectation was positive
demotion_triggers.why: A sharp registered edge almost never digs a 3%-below-turnover hole over 400 bets; a strategy with no edge digs it regularly. The trigger therefore separates a decayed edge from a genuine one without needing to know which it is in advance.
demotion_triggers.arithmetic: P(ROI < -3% over 400 flat bets) = 0.0002 at a true 55% and 0.0061 at breakeven. Because the 55% figure is far below any conventional significance level, the trigger cannot be dismissed as an unlucky streak by a strategy that is merely breaking even.
demotion_triggers.source: computed here from the exact binomial

demotion_triggers.trigger: rolling 200-bet CLV negative for 3 consecutive re-ratings
demotion_triggers.why: CLV is the least noisy skill measure available and is not sensitive to variance in the outcome. Three consecutive negative windows is the standard process-quality failure signal.
demotion_triggers.arithmetic: requires G-5 to be unblocked; cannot fire until prices exist.

demotion_triggers.trigger: documented input defect: any strategy input found to be wrong, unverifiable, or from a source that was later retracted
demotion_triggers.why: A correct result from wrong inputs is not a result. This is the trigger that applies to this repository's own history (a standings transcription had to be corrected once already).
demotion_triggers.arithmetic: n/a - a defect is a defect regardless of sample size

demotion_triggers.trigger: the strategy's own stated dependence term cannot be re-estimated from current data
demotion_triggers.why: For combos and parlays, if the correlation that justified the joint price cannot be recomputed, the price is a guess and the strategy may not stay live.

demotion_triggers.trigger: reward payout would exceed the notional cap before G-3 is met
demotion_triggers.why: Stops a promotion being paid out of a sample too small to justify it.

demotion_policy: Demotion is automatic: any single trigger fires it. No human vote, no override on the same sample.
A demoted strategy returns to paper and may only be re-promoted on a NEW sample that post-dates the demotion, never on the sample that demoted it.
The demotion, its trigger, and the sample are published on the leaderboard page.
Losing a strategy is a normal cost of running many; hiding it is not permitted.
